title: How a hash map finds a key

segments.title: The puzzle
segments.learningGoal: Notice that lookup does not search.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Why can a hash map find one key among a million in one step?

segments.title: Hash, then jump
segments.learningGoal: A hash function maps a key to a bucket index.
segments.visualPlan: World: key -> hash function -> index -> buckets.

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: It never searches. A hash function turns the key into a number.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And that number picks the bucket?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Yes. The index is the hash modulo the bucket count.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does that look like in code?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Python hashes the key, then reads one slot of an array.

segments.title: Collisions
segments.learningGoal: Two keys can share a bucket; the bucket keeps a chain.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Two keys can share a bucket, right?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Right, that is a collision, and the bucket keeps a short chain.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So: hash, jump, check a short chain.

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Quick check. What picks the bucket? The hash, modulo the bucket count.
